# ICP modeling with AI 

**ICP modeling with AI isn’t theory. It’s a practical system for choosing the right accounts, running smarter plays, and proving marketing’s impact.**

This workbook gives you the tools to do exactly that.

You’ll build your ICP signal map, translate it into a tiered engagement strategy, and create an account measurement system that leadership actually pays attention to. Every exercise includes tools, steps, and a concrete deliverable. So by the time you finish, you’ll have the same operational assets used by teams at PartnerStack, Mutiny, Thoropass, and Airbase.

Bring your CRM, your enrichment data, and 20-30 minutes per section.

By the end, you’ll leave with a complete ICP engine you can use tomorrow.

Exercises in this Workshop:

* [Build a complete ICP signal map](#build-a-complete-icp-signal-map)  
* [Build your tiered engagement strategy](#build-your-tiered-engagement-strategy)  
* [Build your full account measurement system](#build-your-full-account-measurement-system) 

# **Build a complete ICP signal map** {#build-a-complete-icp-signal-map}

![][image2]

You’ll identify the traits that make your best customers successful and the traits that consistently predict poor fit. This creates the raw material for a usable ICP definition and the foundation of your scoring model.

| Tools Google Sheets / Excel (to compare customers vs. DQ leads) Your CRM (Salesforce, HubSpot, Pipedrive, etc.) LinkedIn \+ company websites (manual enrichment) Enrichment tools (Apollo, ZoomInfo, Clay, Clearbit \- optional but helpful) ChatGPT or Claude (to classify patterns or summarize findings) |
| :---- |

### **Step 1: Gather your comparison sets** 

Pull two simple lists from your CRM:

**A. Best customers**

Choose 10–20 accounts with strong retention, high expansion, or consistently high ACV.

| *List best customers…* |
| :---- |

**B. Data Qualified’d leads**

Choose 10–20 accounts you intentionally rejected because they were a poor fit.

(Do *not* use churned accounts \- they still bought, so the signal is muddy.)

This contrast is critical. Eric emphasizes that signals only emerge with side-by-side comparison.

| *List Data Qualified’d leads…* |
| :---- |

---

### **Step 2: Enrich both lists** 

Use whatever data sources you have (internal notes, LinkedIn, website, enrichment tools).

Capture at least:

* Company size  
* Industry and sub-industry  
* Markets served  
* Sales motion (sales-led, PLG, hybrid)  
* Team structure (AEs, SDRs, RevOps, Security, etc.)  
* Tech stack (CRM, MAP, relevant category tools)  
* Growth indicators (hiring velocity, expansion, new product lines)

This doesn’t need to be perfect. You’re looking for patterns, not precision.

| A. Best customers | B. Data Qualified’d leads |
| :---- | :---- |
| *Answer here…* | *Answer here…* |

---

### **Step 3: Identify positive fit signals**

Look for traits that keep showing up in your best customers:

Examples:

* Consistent industries or sub-verticals  
* Similar team structure  
* Clear pain points you solve well  
* Shared tech stack patterns  
* Rapid growth or complexity (multiple products, regions, frameworks)

These become “better if…” signals.

| *Positive fit signals…* |
| :---- |

---

### **Step 4: Identify negative fit signals**

Now look at your DQ’d leads and note what they share:

Examples:

* Industries you rarely win  
* Sales motions incompatible with your product  
* Tech stacks that block adoption  
* Business models that always churn

These become “avoid if…” signals.

| *Negative fit signals…* |
| :---- |

---

### **Step 5: Draft your ICP definition**

Use the prompt Eric shared in the session:

**Our offering is best for**

• \[General type of companies\]

**Who are**

• \[In specific situations or motions\]

**They focus on**

• \[Outcomes or priorities your product improves\]

**They struggle with**

• \[Problems you uniquely solve\]

This becomes your qualitative ICP definition.

| Our offering is best for | Who are | They focus on | They struggle with |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| *Answer here…* | *Answer here…* | *Answer here…* | *Answer here…* |

---

### **Step 6: Build your initial signal table**

Create two columns:

**Positive signals (“better if…”)**

**Negative signals (“avoid if…”)**

This table is the raw material for:

* your future 0–100 scoring model  
* SAM mapping  
* GTM prioritization  
* account engagement tiers (A/B/C/D)

| Positive signals (“better if…”) | Negative signals (“avoid if…”) |
| :---- | :---- |
| *Answer here…* | *Answer here…* |

---

## **Deliverables**

A complete ICP signal map containing:

* Best customer list  
* DQ lead list  
* Positive and negative fit signals  
* Draft ICP definition

This completes the groundwork for building your scoring model in the next lesson.

# **Build your tiered engagement strategy**  {#build-your-tiered-engagement-strategy}

![][image2]

You’ll turn your ICP scoring into a practical engagement model. This exercise helps you decide which accounts deserve high-CAC GTM plays, which should stay inbound-only, and how to design focused “1 message, 1 audience, 1 offer” plays for your highest-value segments.

| Tools Google Sheets / Excel (to map tiers and plays) Your CRM (HubSpot, Salesforce, or similar) LinkedIn Ads Manager (for planning audience-based plays) Google Docs / Notion (for drafting messaging) Any enrichment tool you already used (Apollo, ZoomInfo, Clay, Clearbit; optional) |
| :---- |

### **Time needed: 10-15 minutes total**

---

### **Step 1: Bring over your ICP-scored segments** 

From the previous exercise, select:

* 3–5 A-tier segments  
* 3–5 B-tier segments  
* Your C-tier and D-tier buckets

These will anchor your engagement tiers.

| Tier A | Tier B | Tier C | Tier D |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| *Answer here…* | *Answer here…* | *Answer here…* | *Answer here…* |

---

### **Step 2: Assign the right level of GTM effort**

Use Eric’s tiering logic:

**A-tier:**

* Full GTM activation  
* 1:1 or 1:few ABM  
* Sales \+ Marketing \+ Partnerships  
* High CAC appropriate for high ACV

**B-tier:**

* Targeted campaigns  
* Signal-qualified outreach  
* 1:few or vertical-led plays  
* Medium CAC

**C-tier:**

* Passive acquisition only  
* SEO, inbound, PLG, nurture  
* No targeted spend

**D-tier:**

* Inbound only  
* Zero paid, zero outbound, zero ABM

| Passive | Targeted | Full Activation |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| *Answer here…* | *Answer here…* | *Answer here…* |

---

### **Step 3: Design one GTM play for A and B tiers**

Use the “1 Message / 1 Audience / 1 Offer” structure.

**Audience:**

Choose one ICP segment inside A or B.

**Message:**

A specific pain or scenario unique to that audience.

Example from Thoropass: “Experiencing death by audits?”

**Offer:**

A next step that directly solves the pain (framework audit, benchmarking report, teardown).

Define:

* Channels you’ll use  
* Which teams participate  
* Expected CAC level  
* Desired outcome (SQLs, first meeting, pipeline amount)

| Tier A | Tier B |
| :---- | :---- |
| *1 message here…* | *1 message here…* |
| *1 audience here…* | *1 audience here…* |
| *1 offer here…* | *1 offer here…* |

---

## **Step 4: Identify waste**

For C and D tiers:

* List channels, plays, and reps currently wasting time  
* Mark everything that should be paused permanently  
* Define what remains inbound-only

This is where ACV alignment typically exposes overspend.

| Tier C | Tier D |
| :---- | :---- |
| *List channels, plays, and reps currently wasting time here…* | *List channels, plays, and reps currently wasting time here…* |
| *Mark everything that should be paused permanently here…* | *Mark everything that should be paused permanently here…* |
| *Define what remains inbound-only here…* | *Define what remains inbound-only here…* |

---

## **Step 5: Build your final tier map**

Your map should include:

* Definitions for A, B, C, D  
* GTM effort per tier  
* Specific GTM plays for A and B  
* Spend elimination rules for C and D  
* Notes on CAC-to-ACV alignment

| Tier A | Tier B | Tier C | Tier D |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| *Answer here…* | *Answer here…* | *Answer here…* | *Answer here…* |

---

## **Deliverables**

A complete engagement blueprint that shows:

* Which accounts get high-touch activation  
* Which receive targeted plays  
* Which stay inbound-only  
* How ICP Fit translates to real GTM execution

# **Build your full account measurement system**  {#build-your-full-account-measurement-system}

![][image2]

This exercise helps you turn your ICP model into reporting leadership actually pays attention to. You’ll build a weekly Pipeline Weather Report, plus a high-level TAM penetration view that works for exec and board updates.

| Tools Google Sheets / Excel (for weather report \+ penetration tracking) Your CRM (HubSpot, Salesforce, Pipedrive) Dashboard tool (Looker, PowerBI, HubSpot reports \- optional but useful) LinkedIn Ads Manager (for account penetration insights) AI assistant (ChatGPT/Claude for summarizing patterns or writing the report intro) |
| :---- |

### **Time needed: 10-15 minutes total**

---

### **Step 1: Prepare your ICP scoring data**

Collect:

* All accounts in your TAM/SAM  
* Each account’s ICP Fit score  
* Current opportunity stage or last engagement date

Split them into:

* A-tier  
* B-tier  
* C-tier  
* D-tier

This becomes the backbone of all reporting.

| Tier A | Tier B | Tier C | Tier D |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| *Accounts in your TAM/SAM…* | *Accounts in your TAM/SAM…* | *Accounts in your TAM/SAM…* | *Accounts in your TAM/SAM…* |
| *Account’s ICP Fit score…* | *Account’s ICP Fit score…* | *Account’s ICP Fit score…* | *Account’s ICP Fit score…* |
| *Current opportunity stage or last engagement date…* | *Current opportunity stage or last engagement date…* | *Current opportunity stage or last engagement date…* | *Current opportunity stage or last engagement date…* |

---

### **Step 2: Build your Pipeline Weather Report structure**

Create four sections:

1. **Intro**

    2–3 sentences summarizing directionally what happened this week.

| *Answer here…* |
| :---- |

2. **Weather Forecast**

    Label each ICP tier (A and B) as:  
   * **Sunny** (ahead of pace)  
   * **Cloudy** (stable but needs attention)  
   * **Rainy** (pipeline at risk)

| *Answer here…* |
| :---- |

3. **Leading indicators**

    Track week-over-week changes in:  
   * Meetings booked  
   * Accounts showing intent or engagement  
   * Accounts moving stages

| *Answer here…* |
| :---- |

4. **Lagging indicators**

    Track:  
   * Opportunities created  
   * Pipeline value  
   * Closed-won outcomes

Add simple sparklines or arrows to show movement.

| *Answer here…* |
| :---- |

---

### **Step 3: Build your TAM penetration view**

Using your ICP scores:

* Count how many A, B, C, D accounts exist in your TAM  
* Count how many have been:

  * Engaged  
  * Qualified  
  * Created as opportunities  
  * Closed

| Tier A | Tier B | Tier C | Tier D |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| *Accounts in your TAM…* | *Accounts in your TAM…* | *Accounts in your TAM…* | *Accounts in your TAM…* |
| *Engaged…* | *Engaged…* | *Engaged…* | *Engaged…* |
| *Created as opportunities…* | *Created as opportunities…* | *Created as opportunities…* | *Created as opportunities…* |
| *Closed…* | *Closed…* | *Closed…* | *Closed…* |

Calculate:

* **Penetration rate:** engaged accounts / total ICP accounts

| *Answer here…* |
| :---- |

* **Pipeline coverage:** pipeline value / theoretical TAM value

| *Answer here…* |
| :---- |

* **Progression rate:** % moving stage-to-stage

| *Answer here…* |
| :---- |

This is what leadership cares about most.

---

## **Step 4: Add qualitative insights**

Each week, record:

* 2–3 accounts your GTM team broke into

| *Answer here…* |
| :---- |

* A deal story or call snippet (like Tyler from PartnerStack uses)

| *Answer here…* |
| :---- |

* Risks emerging in key segments

| *Answer here…* |
| :---- |

* Wins worth spotlighting

| *Answer here…* |
| :---- |

These build trust and narrative, not just numbers.

---

## **Step 5: Create your executive slide**

Build a 1-slide view showing:

* TAM by ICP tier  
* Penetration by tier  
* Pipeline created this quarter  
* Weather snapshot  
* One-sentence explanation of what’s improved

This becomes your monthly presentation to leadership and board stakeholders.

---

## **Deliverables**

A complete reporting system including:

* Weekly Pipeline Weather Report  
* TAM penetration metrics  
* ICP-based executive slide  
* Qualitative insights library

This reporting system makes your ICP work visible to leadership, and positions you as a strategic operator, not a channel executor.
